column1: # One fact, one owner. Rule 14.
# regex <TAB> owner note <TAB> what the owner is
# A note that is NOT the owner may mention the fact, but the line must LINK the
# owner, which turns a restatement into a citation. A citation sends the next
# reader to the one file allowed to be wrong.
# TWO THINGS THIS FILE LEARNED THE HARD WAY, 20 September.
# 1. Patterns are REGEX and are anchored. The first version used plain
#    substrings and "2,000 EGP" matched inside "42,000 EGP", reporting eight
#    false restatements in TSA Money alone. A check that cries wolf gets
#    ignored, which is worse than no check.
# 2. NOT EVERY REPEATED FACT HAS AN OWNER, and forcing one wrecks the notes.
#    Dates were listed here and the rewrite produced "Friday the date in
#    [[Delivery Register]]" and "Week 1 · 20 to the date in [[Delivery
#    Register]]". A dated delivery plan OWNS dates -- carrying them is the note
#    doing its job, not drift.
#    Dates, product claims and anything else that CHANGES belong to
#    retired.tsv instead: when the value moves, one row there finds all
#    thirteen copies. Ownership is for facts with a single natural home;
#    retirement is for facts that move. Using the wrong one produces either
#    broken prose or a stale vault.
